findings.summary: A carried pull request (closed because a later merge carried its commits) keeps an Open link. It counts as not landed whenever the local landing records are missing.
findings.evidence: In the evidence snapshot, landing 20261110-190847-zw9f lists many job_landing commits, so a carried job is normally named by a landing record and excluded. If the records branch is absent locally, landings read as empty and that safeguard is gone. Two carried jobs on one line with no accepted attempt would then be held by mistake. A simpler fix: set the carried link's state when it is closed as carried. Low impact; the reading accepted 'either source' as the rule.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/scope_guard.rs (Athena::unlanded_jobs); crates/athena-core/src/gh/landing.rs:380-466 (close_carried_prs leaves the earlier link's state as Open)

The assertions do discriminate as designed: D's producer run, the lander count, and the plan refusal reason in test 1, and the attempts counts in the scope_guard tests.

findings.evidence: The existing drain_holds_the_items_that_depend_on_an_item_of_a_paused_line covers only the 'paused' wording. No line_hold test gives a dependent of a held item.

findings.summary: A pull request that is still waiting on checks counts as not landed until it is seen merged, so a line with one rejection plus one waiting PR is held.
findings.evidence: This is stated in the CHANGELOG. A waiting job is merged by `athena land --pr` and is not re-queued as a drain item (drain.rs:145-152), so the hold does not block its landing.

summary: The change works and I'm passing it: the drain now stops retrying a line of work once two attempts did not land, and holds it as "awaiting diagnosis". A line is the scope guard's grouping of a request with its retries and re-asks. The hold counts rejected jobs, failed jobs, and collisions: jobs that passed verification and landed locally but that the host did not take. "Taken by the host" is read from the pull-request link's `state` field (`LinkState::Landed`, through the new `PrLink::taken_by_host`), or from a landing record naming the job. That fixes the critic's findings on both earlier failed plans. The check runs only before an attempt that has no passed job yet, and again after an item's last failure. So an item's own free landing retry is kept. The scope guard's T1-T5 signals use the old grouping unchanged. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` (202 passed, including the six new hold tests, which go through the real `drain::drain` and `drain::plan` on real records) and `cargo test -p athena-core scope_guard` (39 passed). fmt, clippy and the full test suite are Athena's recorded CI results. All six changed files are in the expected deliverables. The CHANGELOG matches the code and names the diagnosis job, line field and status display as follow-ups. I have four small findings. A carried pull request keeps an Open link and would be counted as not landed if the local landing records were missing. Athena's "fails without the fix" runs for criteria 1–3 failed only because the tests did not compile, and criterion 4's was not run. The new wording for items that depend on a held item has no test. A pull request still waiting on checks counts as not landed until it merges, which the CHANGELOG says.
